research_concepts: lineup coverage of structural roles (organizer, shaper, terminal)
separability of role coverage from player talent and role counts
talent control in lineup-level role analysis
role labels derived from play-by-play and graph play-type records
methodological_questions: Can lineup role coverage be separated from talent and role counts when coverage varies within team?
Does talent control behave adequately when role coverage is collinear with talent?
What sample-size and reliability constraints apply to lineup-level role cells from about 421k possessions across 90 team-seasons?
Are the role labels independent of the possession outcomes they are meant to explain (outcome-derived label and leakage risk)?
Do multiple lineup, role and talent cuts require multiplicity control?

historical_evidence.finding: Superstar suppression by lineup and forced play type. Lineup cells cited at n>=30 (e.g., Jokic vs MIN PPP gap -0.385, n=59). The record notes no placebo or matching, and that later sequence work treated similar star-chain gaps as artifacts. Mechanism recorded as unclear.
Observed on-ball defensive scheme labels from matchup/PBP fields. Labeled rates were 14.9% (DET, 10 of 67) and 3.3% (ORL, 2 of 60). The switches_on field was unpopulated. Recorded as a failed gate.

Player-level BEST vs AVOID H2 PPP gaps (exploratory) across 78 players with at least 5 rows per tier. Several extreme gaps rest on very small n (e.g., D. Lively II +1.833 at n=6/6). Some reverse signs. Recorded as lacking a multiplicity or clustered test.

Player-level BEST vs AVOID PPP gap on initiator-filtered H2 possessions (55 series). Mean gap +0.427 PPP (n>=10 per tier). Only 3 players reached n>=30 in both tiers. Recorded limitation: small_sample.
Player BEST/AVOID tier tendency in H2 trigger games: team AVOID% ranged 50.6% (ORL) to 6.8% (SAC); player samples 10-178 possessions. Recorded as descriptive with no outcome test.
Joint vs sequential Rank-then-Route ranking over n=2,779 triggers. Joint pick matched sequential in 80.3%. Mean PPP left on table was +0.020 overall. Recorded as descriptive.

Defensive scheme change within and across games from inferred labels. Within-game change 61.0%, cross-game change 67.7%, and transition matrices near-uniform. The record states that the inferred label cannot separate defensive adjustment from offense executing differently, and that near-uniform matrices are consistent with label noise.
Play-type classifier assisted-flag leak: SPOT_UP showed 2.83 PPP because the assisted flag exists only on makes. After rewrite, SPOT_UP was about 1.16 and TRANSITION about 1.20.

Three-level counter ranking (population, team, matchup). Best counter after a suppressed play type was not stable across levels (for example, MIA disagreed with the league-level DRIVE ranking). L1 n_mu ranged 5 to 696; playoff matchups 4 to 44. Recorded risks: mechanical floor and small sample.

Superstar sequential suppression by the opponent's preceding play. PUTBACK was top suppressor for 6+ stars (e.g., D. Mitchell d=-0.294, n_after=95; B. Beal d=-0.345, n=32). Recorded as having no multiplicity correction and n_after of 32-95 in several cells.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Labelling on-ball defensive coverage (DROP/ICE/SWITCH) from matchup and PBP fields to create a usable role or scheme variable.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as failed_gate. Confident label rates were 14.9% and 3.3%, the switches_on field did not populate, and the record cites label error and small sample.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Inferring possession-level play types from PBP for use as a predictor of points.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as C_artifact. The assisted flag existed only on makes, which inflated SPOT_UP to 2.83 PPP. The effect was produced by label construction, not by play structure.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Using inferred defensive scheme labels to detect within-game and cross-game scheme change.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as untestable. The label cannot separate defensive adjustment from offensive execution, and near-uniform transition matrices are consistent with label noise.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Counter ranking that was expected to be stable from population to team to matchup level.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as inconclusive. Rankings disagreed across levels, and the record cites mechanical floor and small sample.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Identifying star-specific lineup and forced-play suppressors in the possession graph.
failed_approaches.why: No placebo or matching was used, and later sequence work treated similar gaps as artifacts (recorded as RISK:PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE; mechanism unclear).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Player-level BEST/AVOID gap estimates from single-game playsheets.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as small n per player, no multiplicity or clustered test, and some sign reversals. The record classifies the question as unanswerable with that design.

evidence_establishes: No retrieved record tests lineup coverage of organizer, shaper or terminal roles, nor whether that coverage varies within team, is separable from talent or role counts, or leaves talent control well-behaved.

Across the retrieved records, play-type and scheme labels built from PBP or graph records have repeatedly shown label error, classifier leakage or unstable rankings (SF-PAP-096, SF-APPS-058, SF-APPA-005, SF-APPM-055).
Lineup- and player-level cells are frequently small: many cells sit below n>=30, and only a few star cells reach that threshold (SF-CHT-009, SF-APPS-036, SF-APPA-050).
Multiplicity and placebo controls were absent in several earlier families, so their reported gaps are not reliable evidence of structure (SF-CHT-009, SF-APPA-048, SF-APPA-050).
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether organizer, shaper and terminal roles can be defined operationally from this data. None of the retrieved records defines them.
Whether role coverage is separable from talent. No retrieved record fits a model with both.
Whether talent control behaves under within-team variation in coverage.
The reliability of any role measure at the lineup level.
Whether any earlier record of this project studies the same question. The retrieved set is adjacent, not identical.
own_inferences: The research question is underspecified: 'talent control behaves' has no stated criterion, and the role definitions are absent from the task statement.

If roles are derived from play-type or graph records, the labels may be functions of the same possession outcomes used as the response (OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL), which would make the separability claim partly circular.
Coverage and talent are likely collinear at the lineup level, since starters and high-usage players tend to carry the roles, so separability needs an explicit identification argument.
With 90 team-seasons and within-team lineup cells, the effective sample for the coverage effect is likely limited by lineup-level exposure, not possession count.
uncertainties: The operational definitions and thresholds for organizer, shaper and terminal roles.
The number of lineups with adequate exposure in each role-coverage category.
How the graph-derived play-type records were generated, and whether they use the outcome.
Whether the talent measure is independent of the role labels.
Whether a related but separate project study exists that was not returned. Only one retrieval was made, and the result set is adjacent.

historical_effect.explanation: Before retrieval the question looked testable with the available per-game files. The retrieved records show a repeated pattern: play-type and scheme labels built from PBP have leaked, been noisy or been unstable across levels; lineup and player cells are often underpowered; and placebo and multiplicity controls were usually missing. Given that record, the design must first fix role definitions and validate them against outcome-independent inputs before any test of coverage, separability or talent control. That moved the decision from proceeding directly to a conditional recommendation not to proceed until those steps are in place.

blocking_constraints.text: Organizer, shaper and terminal labels may be derived from the same play-type records and possession outcomes used as the response, so coverage and outcome are not separable without an outcome-independent definition.
Role labels from PBP and graph records have shown label error and classifier leakage in earlier families (SF-APPS-058, SF-PAP-096, SF-APPA-005); reliability of lineup-level role coverage is unknown.
Within-team lineup cells with adequate exposure in each coverage category are likely sparse; several earlier cells fell below n>=30 (SF-APPS-036, SF-APPA-050).
Coverage is likely collinear with talent and role counts at the lineup level, so separability depends on an explicit identification strategy that is not yet specified.
Only 90 team-seasons are available, and within-team coverage variation may be too narrow to detect a coverage effect at useful power.

prior_work.summary: No retrieved record tests lineup coverage of organizer, shaper or terminal roles or its separability from talent. Adjacent records cover play-type and defensive-scheme labels, counter rankings and star suppressors. They are relevant because they show label error, leakage, sparse cells and missing multiplicity control in this project's prior work, and they are not answers to the question posed.

risks.text: Role labels may use the same possession outcomes as the response, making the coverage-to-outcome relationship partly circular.
Graph play-type records built from the full play-by-play may encode post-possession information into role labels (cf. SF-PAP-096 assisted-flag leak).
Role and scheme labels from matchup and PBP fields have shown high noise or low coverage (SF-APPS-058, SF-APPA-005).
Lineup-level role coverage may be unreliable across seasons or samples; no reliability estimate exists in the retrieved records.
Many lineup-by-coverage cells may have too few possessions to estimate reliably within team.
90 team-seasons with within-team variation may not provide power to detect a coverage effect after talent control.
Talent, starter status, usage and role counts are likely correlated with coverage, so the separability claim is not identified without an explicit strategy.
Selecting lineups or teams with high or low coverage by outcome may produce regression to the mean in the coverage-performance relationship.
Earlier star-chain and suppression results lacked placebo or matching controls (SF-CHT-009, SF-APPA-048), so any role effect would need placebo checks.
Many lineup, role and talent cuts were used in earlier families without correction (SF-APPA-050, SF-APPA-048); the same risk applies here.
Seasons 2022-23 through 2025-26 and playoff splits may shift in role usage and rules; the 2025-26 data is partial before the stated completion dates.

design.estimand: Within-team association between lineup coverage of at least one organizer, shaper or terminal role and lineup-level offensive PPP, conditional on a talent measure that is shown to be separable from coverage. This estimand is not fully defined until role labels are fixed.
design.unit: Lineup-game or lineup-season cell nested within team-season, with possessions as the measurement base.
design.sample: Regular season 2022-23 to 2024-25 as the development sample. 2025-26 regular season, using only games after 2026-04-13 for the confirmatory check. Playoffs are excluded from the primary test. All 90 team-seasons are candidates.
design.power: Not computed. Before any test, run a simulation of coverage effect detectability at the lineup-cell level with the observed exposure distribution. Require at least 30 possessions per coverage category within team for a cell to be included, and report the number of cells surviving this gate.
design.controls: Talent measured from out-of-sample or lagged data, not from the same season's outcomes. Starter status, minutes share and usage as covariates. Team-season fixed effects. Clustered standard errors by team-season. A separability check: report the variance inflation of coverage given talent and role counts, and the partial correlation between them. Role labels must be built from an outcome-independent input, for example pre-possession alignment or pre-registered event types, and validated against a hand-labeled sample before use.
design.falsification: A placebo role (random or outcome-independent relabelling of the same possessions) should show no association with PPP. A lagged coverage measure should not predict the current-season residual after talent control. Failing either check counts as evidence of confounding or leakage.
design.multiplicity: Pre-register one primary coefficient (coverage of at least one role). Treat other roles, cuts and playoff splits as secondary with Holm correction across all reported tests.
design.decision_rule: Proceed to a confirmatory claim only if: (1) role labels pass a hand-label validation check with stated agreement; (2) at least a predefined number of lineup cells per coverage category survive the exposure gate; (3) the placebo and lagged checks are null; (4) the primary coefficient survives Holm correction at the pre-registered alpha, with a confidence interval reported. Otherwise report as inconclusive or untestable.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game files for 2022-23 to 2024-25 regular seasons and playoffs, plus 2025-26 regular season complete from 2026-04-13. Graph-derived play-type records are excluded from role construction unless their generation is audited for outcome use. Record the data snapshot date.

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- search_documents(query): rank further study-family documents by text relevance; returns up to 10 families not yet returned.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

messages.content:
Research question (as posed on 2026-07-13, in the area of structural roles and influence):
Lineup coverage (>=1 organizer, shaper, terminal) varies within team, is separable from talent/counts, and talent control behaves.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 420,993 possessions; 90 team-seasons

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.
